title: Book One · Chapter 176: The Bent Bridge
story:
The little boy likes the river.

He likes the blue line on the map. He likes the little boats beside it. Most of all, he likes the paper bridge.

“Can a boat go under?”

“A small one,” Ronan says.

The boy puts his face close to the table.

“Can I see?”

Ronan moves one paper boat. It goes under the bridge and comes out on the other side.

The boy laughs.

Then his bag catches the corner of the map.

The paper lifts. The bridge tips over. One boat falls to the floor.

Ronan catches the edge with both hands.

“Wait!”

The little boy stands still. His smile is gone.

The older girl takes hold of his bag and moves it away from the table.

“I’m sorry,” she says.

Ronan looks at the bridge. One side is flat now. A long fold crosses the blue river.

People have stopped to look. Ronan feels hot and wants to hide the bent part.

“It is all right,” he starts to say.

But it is not all right yet.

He takes a breath.

“We need to fix this part.”

Mei comes over. She does not ask about the child. She looks at the bent bridge first. She puts her box on the floor and looks closely.

“Hold this end.”

Ronan holds it. Leo moves the boat from the floor to the table.

Miss Wu asks the visitors to give them a little room.

The small boy puts both hands behind his back. His eyes look wet.

Ronan once broke something too. He felt bad then. He wants to help this boy. He does not want the boy to cry.

“You can stand here,” he tells him. “Your bag can go by the wall.”

“I broke it.”

“One part. Not all of it.”

Mei gently opens the folded side of the bridge. The paper stood straight before. Now it bends to one side.

“We have more paper,” Leo says.

“There isn’t time to make the whole thing again.”

“Just a support,” Mei says.

She folds a short strip. Ronan keeps the map still while she puts the strip inside the bridge.

They lift their hands slowly.

The bridge stands.

It has a little line across the top. Ronan can see it. Everyone can see it.

The river on the map is still folded at the edge.

Mei puts a clean sheet under it. Leo brings the small stone back. They smooth the corner and put the stone down.

“We can move the map farther in,” Ronan says.

They make room at the front of the table. Now a bag cannot catch the same corner so easily.

The little boy is still watching.

“Does the boat go under?” he asks in a very small voice.

Ronan picks up the paper boat.

“Let’s see.”

He sends it under the bridge. It comes out the other side.

The boy gives a small smile.

Ronan hands him an empty sheet from Mei’s box.

“You can draw a boat. Here, on the other table.”

He looks at Mei first. She nods.

The older girl takes the boy to the clear table. Soon, he is drawing a very large boat with three windows.

Ronan looks back at the map.

Mei is pressing the new support into place. Leo is showing another visitor the street names.

Ronan wants to thank them, but Mei speaks first.

“Next time, more space round the edge.”

“Yes.”

“And perhaps a stronger bridge.”

“We can do that.”

The visitors begin walking round the room again. Some go to the pictures. Others stay by the map.

Ronan stays by the table until his hands stop shaking. Then he goes to meet the next person at the door.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达
- tip over：倾倒。
- support：支撑物。
- strip：细长的一条。
- gently：轻轻地。

## 理解
1. 展示出了什么问题？三个孩子怎样分工？
2. 修好后，他们怎样减少再次发生同类问题的可能？
